He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]]. ==Early life== Lewis was born and grew up in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]] and initially attended [[Calvert Hall College High School]].{{cite web|first=Glenn|last=Graham|title=Calvert Hall freshman Justin Lewis selected to participate in USA basketball camp|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/high-school/bal-calvert-hall-freshman-justin-lewis-selected-to-participate-in-usa-basketball-camp-20160922-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210623151741/https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/high-school/bal-calvert-hall-freshman-justin-lewis-selected-to-participate-in-usa-basketball-camp-20160922-story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 23, 2021|date=September 22, 2016|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|access-date=October 31, 2023}} He transferred to the [[Baltimore Polytechnic Institute]] after his freshman year.{{cite web|first=Glenn|last=Graham|title=Former Poly star Justin Lewis off to thrilling start with Marquette|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2020/12/11/former-poly-star-justin-lewis-off-to-thrilling-start-with-marquette-big-time-player-making-big-time-plays/|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=December 11, 2020|access-date=October 31, 2023}} As a junior, Lewis averaged 17.3 points and 9.2 rebounds per game with 16 double doubles and was named first team All-Metro and second team All-Maryland by ''[[USA Today]]'' as Baltimore Polytechnic won the state championship.{{cite web|title=Poly basketball star Justin Lewis commits to Marquette|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2019/07/24/poly-basketball-star-justin-lewis-commits-to-marquette/|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=July 24, 2019|access-date=October 29, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 19.3 points, 13.4 rebounds and 4.4 blocks per game and was named the Metro Co-player of the Year and first-team All-Maryland while leading the team to a second straight state championship.{{cite web|title=Players of the year: Adrian Baldwin & Justin Lewis|url=https://digitaledition.baltimoresun.com/tribune/article_popover.aspx?guid=541fe923-a051-4745-b38e-a78e1ac27b9a|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029212119/https://digitaledition.baltimoresun.com/tribune/article_popover.aspx?guid=541fe923-a051-4745-b38e-a78e1ac27b9a|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 29, 2021|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=March 31, 2020|access-date=October 29, 2021}} A four-star recruit, Lewis committed to playing college basketball for [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] over offers from [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], among others.{{cite web|first=Evan|last=Daniels|title=Four-star forward Justin Lewis commits to Marquette |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Justin-Lewis-Marquette-Four-Star-Commit-133878375/|website=[[247Sports]]|date=July 24, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2021}} ==College career== Lewis came off (and on) the bench for Marquette as a freshman.{{cite web|title=Marquette has freshmen stars in Dawson Garcia and Justin Lewis|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2021/01/15/marquette-has-freshmen-stars-dawson-garcia-and-justin-lewis/4166717001/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=January 15, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}} He averaged 7.8 points and 5.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|title=Shaka Smart is bringing new energy to Marquette. He's built for that.|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2021/10/13/new-coach-shaka-smart-instilling-culture-at-marquette/6033194001/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Marquette's Justin Lewis hopes to be NBA player under Shaka Smart|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2021/10/28/marquettes-justin-lewis-hopes-nba-player-under-shaka-smart/8549918002/|url-access=subscription|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 29, 2021}} On January 26, 2022, Lewis scored a career-high 33 points as well as nine rebounds and six assists in a 73–63 win against [[2021–22 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]].{{cite news|title=Freshman Lewis scores 33, No. 22 Marquette beats Seton Hall|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373563|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=February 8, 2022}} He was named to the First Team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]], as well as [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Big East Most Improved Player]].{{cite web|title=Forward also All-BIG EAST First Team selection|url=https://gomarquette.com/news/2022/3/7/mens-basketball-justin-lewis-named-big-east-most-improved-player|work=[[Marquette Golden Eagles]]|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=March 10, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Windy City Bulls (2023)=== After becoming undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Lewis signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on July 7, 2022{{cite web|title=Bulls Sign Terry, Freeman-Liberty. Lewis inked to a Two-Way deal|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-terry-freeman-liberty-lewis-inked-to-a-two-way-deal|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2022|access-date=October 8, 2023}} and afterwards joined them in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612741/bulls|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2022}} In his Summer League debut, Lewis scored eight points and five rebounds in a 100–99 win against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|title=Dallas Mavericks vs Chicago Bulls Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/dal-vs-chi-1522200003/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2022|access-date=July 14, 2022}} Justin Lewis tore his ACL and was later waived on October 15 while he rehabbed the injury.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bulls Cut Carlik Jones, Okaro White|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/10/bulls-cut-carlik-jones-okaro-white.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=October 8, 2023}} On March 7, 2023, Lewis signed another two-way contract with the Chicago Bulls,{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Justin Lewis to Two-Way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-justin-lewis-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} but was waived on December 16, after appearing in 12 games with the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls sign Henri Drell to Two-Way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-sign-henri-drell-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2023|access-date=December 17, 2023}} Two days later, he returned to Windy City.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Windy City Bulls Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Windy-City-Bulls/44/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 3, 2024}} ===Salt Lake City Stars (2023–2024)=== On December 27, 2023, Lewis was traded to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite web|title=SLC Stars Acquire Justin Lewis from Windy City Bulls|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/slc-stars-acquire-justin-lewis-from-windy-city-bulls/n-6042665|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 27, 2023|access-date=January 3, 2024}} ===Calgary Surge (2024)=== On May 1, 2024, Lewis signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Calgary Surge Sign Forward Justin Lewis|url=https://www.cebl.ca/calgary-surge-sign-forward-justin-lewis|website=CEBL.ca|date=May 1, 2024|access-date=May 2, 2024}} However, he was waived on July 22. ===Return to Salt Lake City (2024)=== On October 13, 2024, Lewis signed with the [[Utah Jazz]],{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Justin Lewis|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-justin-lewis|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}} but was waived three days later.{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Waive Justin Lewis|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-justin-lewis|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 16, 2024}} On October 28, he rejoined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite web|title=Stars Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster/n-6160474|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 2, 2024}} ===Delaware Blue Coats (2025)=== On February 20, 2025, Lewis was acquired by the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] in exchange for player rights of [[Rob Edwards (basketball)|Rob Edwards]] as well as a 2025 second-round pick in the [[NBA G League]] draft.{{cite web |title=Sixers' G League Team Strikes Trade with Utah Jazz Affiliate |url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/sixers-g-league-team-strikes-trade-with-utah-jazz-affiliate-01jmjhgmm0wk |website=Philadelphia 76ers On SI |access-date=21 February 2025 |date=21 February 2025}} ===Limoges CSP (2025–present)=== On August 7, 2025, he signed with [[Limoges CSP]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.limogescsp.com/actualites-details/justin-lewis-2026.html|title=Justin
